subject: Biotechnology
title: CHO Cell Culture
description: A fast breakdown of CHO Cell Culture for builders.

hook.text: Chinese hamster ovary cells produce over 70% of all biopharmaceuticals — the unsung heroes of modern medicine.

buildup.text: CHO cells grow in suspension culture — massive stainless-steel bioreactors hold up to 20,000 liters.

discovery.text: CHO cells fold human proteins correctly and add proper sugar chains — bacteria cannot do this.

twist.text: Developing a stable CHO cell line takes 6 to 12 months — finding the best producer among millions of clones.

climax.text: Modern CHO cells produce over 10 grams of antibody per liter — a 100-fold improvement in 30 years.

punchline.text: Tiny hamster cells in giant tanks — the factory behind most biologics.

quiz.question: Why are CHO cells preferred over bacteria for producing most biopharmaceuticals?
options: CHO cells grow faster than any bacterial strain
CHO cells correctly fold proteins and add sugar modifications that bacteria cannot
Bacteria are too dangerous to use in pharmaceutical manufacturing

details.summary: Chinese hamster ovary cells are the dominant production platform for therapeutic antibodies and proteins, manufacturing over 70 percent of all biopharmaceuticals. Their popularity stems from human-compatible protein folding, stable genetics, and decades of regulatory acceptance.
details.whyItMatters: CHO cells are the workhorse of the biopharmaceutical industry. Understanding their biology and engineering is essential for producing safe, effective biologics at scale, directly impacting drug availability and cost for patients worldwide.
takeaways: CHO cells produce over 70 percent of all biopharmaceutical proteins
They add human-compatible sugar modifications essential for drug function
Decades of regulatory history make CHO the default platform for biologics

faq.question: Why are Chinese hamster ovary cells preferred over human cells?
faq.answer: CHO cells grow well in suspension culture, tolerate genetic manipulation, and add protein sugar modifications similar to but distinct from human patterns. Importantly, human viruses cannot replicate in CHO cells, adding a safety layer against viral contamination.

faq.question: How many antibody molecules can a CHO cell produce?
faq.answer: Modern engineered CHO cell lines can produce 5 to 10 grams of antibody per liter of culture, up from milligrams per liter decades ago. This thousand-fold improvement came through cell line engineering, media optimization, and process development over four decades.
